questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth several times. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding during the day?

options.text: Neither your low beam nor high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This provides the best visibility.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits lower with a passenger because of the extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust the brake light position.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Avoid the center of the lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: What benefit does wearing a riding jacket provide in hot weather?

options.text: It helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
It is not recommended because it causes heat-related problems.
It should only be worn if it is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly if a vehicle is following you too closely. The driver behind you may not see hazards ahead that you are slowing for.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue when riding, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least once every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you may feel extreme fatigue.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans into a turn, some tire grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either brake lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, braking pressure goes to both brakes. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is following too closely. The other driver may not notice the hazard ahead that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are about to slow down where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle just before hitting the object to lighten the front end.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run parallel to the road?

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: To safely cross railroad tracks or seams parallel to your lane, move your position so you cross at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn. If you try to cross slowly, the tracks could catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting difficult.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. A high beam reflects off these conditions and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. This applies to all stops, including normal ones.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: When you need to brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and reapply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and reapply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up from braking, release the front brake immediately and reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake firmly while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.
